divisions.description: The alert experience itself: signal feeds you control, confidence-ranked alerts, and delivery to the people who need to act. Designed to be calm by default and unmistakable when it counts.

features.body: Connect the sources you already rely on and decide exactly what gets watched, how closely, and by whom. Nothing is monitored that you didn't choose.
features.title: Signal feeds you control

features.body: Every incoming signal is deduplicated, checked against a second source where possible, and ranked by urgency and confidence before it can interrupt anyone.
features.title: Confidence-ranked alerts

features.body: Urgent signals break through instantly. Everything else arrives as a calm digest in the channels your team already uses — no new dashboard to babysit.
features.title: Delivery where people are

features.body: If the first person doesn't respond, the alert moves on — quietly, on a schedule you set. Never a blast to everyone, never a siren for a blip.
features.title: Escalation that respects people

divisions.label: Core product
divisions.longDescription: Omnilert App is where signals become decisions. You connect the sources you already rely on, set what matters and how much, and the App does the watching — deduplicating, cross-checking, and ranking everything that comes in. What reaches you is short and specific: what happened, how sure we are, and what to do next. Everything else waits quietly in a digest you can read when you choose to.
divisions.name: Omnilert App
divisions.tagline: The product people use every day

divisions.description: The research and experiments side of the company: prototypes, detection methods, and field notes from building in public. Lab work that proves itself graduates into the App; the rest stays a lesson.

features.body: New ways of spotting weak signals early — tested in the open, measured honestly, and only promoted when they beat what's already live.
features.title: Detection prototypes

features.body: We study how people actually respond to alerts over time, and design against the cry-wolf effect: an ignored alert is a failed alert.
features.title: Alert-fatigue research

features.body: Write-ups of experiments as they happen — the hypothesis, the result, and the lesson — published in the updates feed below.
features.title: Field notes, in public

features.body: Lab work that proves itself becomes an App feature. The rest stays a documented lesson, so the same mistake is never paid for twice.
features.title: A graduation path to the App

divisions.label: R&D
divisions.longDescription: Omnilert Lab is the company's workshop. It's where detection methods are prototyped, alert-fatigue research happens, and half-formed ideas get tested against reality before they can touch the product people rely on. Lab publishes its notes as it goes — what was tried, what broke, and what earned its way into the App. If the App is the promise, the Lab is how the promise keeps getting better.
divisions.name: Omnilert Lab
divisions.tagline: Where the next version is figured out

settings.about_body: Most alert tools shout. Omnilert observes. We collect signals from the sources you choose, weigh them the way a careful analyst would — what changed, how sure are we, who needs to know — and deliver one precise message. The draft positioning on this page is a starting point: every word here is editable from the Control Room, so the story can sharpen as the product does.
settings.about_title: Built like an observatory, not an alarm bell.
settings.div_cta_body: Early access opens division by division. Tell us what you'd want watched and we'll bring you in as soon as there's a seat.
settings.footer_note: Omnilert is an independent startup in active development. This site is a working draft — positioning is being refined with early users.
settings.hero_subtitle: Omnilert watches the signals around your team — and turns noise into a short, clear alert you can act on. No feeds to babysit, no dashboards to decode. When something needs you, you hear about it. When it doesn't, we stay quiet.
settings.hero_title: Every signal that matters. One quiet place to see it.
settings.how_1_body: Point Omnilert at the sources you already rely on. You choose what is watched and how closely — nothing is monitored that you didn't ask for.
settings.how_2_body: Incoming signals are deduplicated, checked for confidence, and ranked by urgency, so a routine blip never looks like an emergency — and a real emergency never looks routine.
settings.how_3_body: The right people get a short message that says what happened, why it matters, and what to do next. Delivered where they already are.

updates.body: Our first design principle for alerts: an alert that cries wolf trains people to ignore it. We're prototyping confidence-ranked delivery — urgent signals break through instantly, everything else arrives as a digest. Early notes and results will appear here.
updates.title: Lab note: calm is a feature

updates.body: The old site was a placeholder README. This new home — dark Ventriloc observatory style, one ember of orange — is built to grow with the company: every section is controlled from our own backend, so the story can evolve as fast as the product does.
